notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on matplotlib/matplotlib at parent commit 2d87c9584499f7619b3c84b89121a27c80d2373e (real upstream issue #30007, fixed upstream by 91740933b658437016063f904030706d84b4502b). Axes.pie with wedge sizes that are all zero divides by zero during normalization, leaves NaN wedge angles, and the call dies deep inside the path-construction/arc code with 'ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer' instead of a clear user-facing error; the upstream fix adds a `if sx == 0: raise ValueError('All wedge sizes are zero')` guard right after sx = x.sum() in Axes.pie, plus the regression test test_pie_all_zeros (appended to lib/matplotlib/tests/test_axes.py). Difficulty deliberately raised vs the upstream pool: the reproduction is NOT given. The instruction describes only the user-visible symptom and the desired clear error, and requires the agent to first write its own failing reproduction script at /app/reproduce.py (contract: exit 0 + print REPRO-OK only when the pie call raises ValueError whose message contains 'All wedge sizes are zero'; any other outcome prints the observed behaviour and exits nonzero). The verifier then runs the agent's own repro twice - against the pre-fix tree concept (repo HEAD blob restored for lib/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py, repro must exit nonzero and report the NaN symptom) and against the repaired tree (repro must exit 0 with REPRO-OK) - proving the repro bites in both directions, then copies in the hash-pinned fix-commit test_axes.py (golden) and requires test_pie_all_zeros to pass, runs nine of the project's own existing pie tests that do not use image comparison (test_pie_textprops, test_pie_get_negative_values, test_pie_invalid_explode/labels/radius, test_normalize_kwarg_pie, test_pie_hatch_single, test_pie_hatch_multi, test_pie_non_finite_values) to prove nothing else broke, and runs two authored hidden cases whose inputs the upstream test never uses: all-zero wedge inputs of other shapes (3 slices, numpy zeros array, labelled) and all-zero inputs with explode/startangle/counterclock/autopct keyword paths, each required to raise the clean message, plus sanity that non-zero pies still render. Image: single-commit clone (git init + git fetch --depth 1 origin <parent>; rev-list --all --count == 1; fix commit object never fetched into the working clone, only into a throwaway clone deleted at build time), meson editable install (pip install --no-build-isolation -e ., freetype/harfbuzz/qhull vendored subprojects compiled at build time), deps fully pinned (pyparsing 3.1.4 < 3.2.0 so collection does not abort on the resetCache deprecation under warnings-as-errors; pytest 8.4.2; numpy 2.5.3; meson-python 0.16.0; pybind11 3.1.0; ninja 1.13.2; meson 1.12.0; contourpy 1.3.3; kiwisolver 1.5.1; cycler 0.12.1; fonttools 4.65.0; packaging 26.3; certifi 2026.7.22; pillow 12.3.0; python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0; setuptools-scm 10.2.3; setuptools 84.0.0), thread pools pinned to 1. Measured on bench-base:python-3.12 (Debian trixie, python 3.12.13): full from-scratch editable build 123 s wall with 64 cores on the host (layer #8), final image 1.34 GB total / 648 MB unique; prior-wave matplotlib tasks used the same 5400 build_timeout on this host and passed. Build-time smokes proved the image ships the mined failing state (ax.pie([0,0]) raises 'cannot convert float NaN to integer' and no 'All wedge sizes are zero' message; the golden test FAILS on the parent tree).
